rows.title: Analyzing 2019: Unrest on the Texas-Mexico border
rows.standfirst: The immigration and humanitarian crisis continues at the Texas-Mexico border, where things have persistently been made worse by harsh government policies.

rows.title: In rural Texas, people experiencing homelessness lead “masked” lives outside of public view
rows.standfirst: Homeless Texans in the state’s less populated areas are harder for people to find and help. But the number of people experiencing homelessness outside of Texas’ urban centers has increased 33% in recent years.

rows.title: Julián Castro drops out of presidential race
rows.standfirst: Castro’s departure means there will be no Texans competing in the Democratic presidential primary.

rows.title: What you need to know about Texas’ new surprise medical billing law
rows.standfirst: The law aims to remove patients from billing disputes between health plans and doctors, but it only applies to the 16% of Texans with state-regulated health insurance.

rows.title: Texas judge tells Fort Worth hospital it can remove baby from life support
rows.standfirst: Tinslee Lewis’ family plans to appeal the judge’s decision, according to Texas Right to Life.

rows.title: Texas A&M University president applied for a job at University of Colorado
rows.standfirst: The president of the University of Texas at El Paso and the former Texas Tech University System chancellor were also on the short list for the top position at the University of Colorado System.

rows.title: In his presidential campaign, Julián Castro stood out but couldn’t break out
rows.standfirst: The former U.S. housing secretary and San Antonio mayor ended his White House bid Thursday after failing to see efforts to distinguish himself translate into reliable support.

rows.title: Analyzing 2019: Elections past, elections future
rows.standfirst: Election results from 2018 and prospects for the 2020 election led by President Donald Trump’s reelection bid provided a steady and strong undertow for political and policy conversations in Texas. And they still do.

rows.title: Marijuana prosecutions in Texas have dropped by more than half since lawmakers legalized hemp
rows.standfirst: After Texas legalized hemp and threw marijuana prosecution into chaos last year, prosecutors filed far fewer criminal charges, police departments paid for private testing and public crime labs were struggling to catch up.

rows.title: After a man died, Greg Abbott blamed Austin’s homeless policies. The mayor called it demonizing.
rows.standfirst: A fatal stabbing near downtown Austin on Friday has reignited a social media squabble between Abbott and Austin leaders over the city’s decision to overhaul its homeless policies.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas elections aren’t starting now — they’re already running at full speed
rows.standfirst: Candidates and campaigns start the year at full speed, sprinting their way to primary election voting that begins in less than two months. It’s the start of what should be a momentous and turbulent presidential election year.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott remains quiet on whether the state will opt out of refugee program
rows.standfirst: It’s still unclear if Abbott will join nearly 40 other governors who have decided to stay in the program.

rows.title: Joe Biden endorses Democrat in battleground Texas House special election
rows.standfirst: The leading Democratic presidential candidate is wading into the Jan. 28 special election runoff for House District 28.

rows.title: Julián Castro endorses Elizabeth Warren days after ending presidential campaign
rows.standfirst: The former U.S. housing secretary and San Antonio mayor says there’s “one candidate I see who’s unafraid to fight like hell to make sure America’s promise will be there for everyone.”

rows.title: Tzintzún Ramirez deals with back-to-back criticism in Democratic primary to challenge Cornyn
rows.standfirst: The candidate has had to confront backlash to two episodes in recent days: comments about her Mexican heritage and an endorsement from actress Susan Sarandon.

rows.title: National Democrats jump into new lawsuit over Texas voter registration requirements
rows.standfirst: Sensing opportunity in 2020, the Texas Democratic Party and campaign arms for Democrats in the U.S. House and Senate are ramping up legal challenges to voting restrictions, this time arguing that the state is unconstitutionally rejecting voter registration applications with digital signatures.

rows.title: Suburban Texas councilman faces recall after declaring a “black state of emergency” over police shootings
rows.standfirst: Over 3,000 people, including McKinney’s mayor and three members of the City Council, have signed a petition to recall La’Shadion Shemwell. He is the the lone black member on the council.

rows.title: Analysis: Julián Castro’s unsuccessful bid for president wasn’t really an ending
rows.standfirst: It’s possible for a political candidate to win by losing — to rise in prominence as a result of a losing campaign for office. Beto O’Rourke tried and failed to do that. But keep an eye on Julián Castro, whose profile rose as his presidential bid fell apart.

rows.title: National Democrats target Republican candidate over a child abuse case in battleground state House race
rows.standfirst: A Democratic super PAC is unveiling a TV ad that focuses on decades-old accusations authorities dropped against Gary Gates, the Republican running against Democrat Eliz Markowitz in the nationally watched contest for Texas House District 28.

rows.title: Former Castro supporters in Texas switch to Biden after Castro drops out
rows.standfirst: The new endorsements come a day after Castro, who ended his campaign last week, threw his support to one of Biden’s opponents, Elizabeth Warren.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott warns Texas agencies seeing 10,000 attempted cyber attacks per minute from Iran
rows.standfirst: State agencies are seeing an increase in cyber security threats as Iranian officials vow revenge against the U.S. for killing a top general.

rows.title: He spent a month in Texas jail accused of hauling 3,350 pounds of marijuana. But lab results say it was legal hemp.
rows.standfirst: The man had told a Texas Department of Public Safety trooper that his truck contained hemp, not weed. He was released from detention after a federal crime lab tested the cargo.

rows.title: An open-government mystery solved: McAllen paid Enrique Iglesias $485,000 for 2015 performance
rows.standfirst: The pop star’s contract with the city — long hidden by what critics described as gaping holes in the state’s open-records laws — became public this week after new legislation governing the public’s right to know went into effect.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Watch five experts predict the future of health care in Texas
rows.standfirst: In this edition of Tenth Talks, a Texas Tribune video series on the next 10 years of Texas, five of the state’s top health industry innovators predict what’s in store for their field.

rows.title: TribCast: A look ahead at the 2020 political landscape in Texas
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Evan, Cassi and Matthew about the political year ahead with heated battles for the Texas House and the state’s 38 electoral votes.

rows.title: Dallas neighborhood established by freed slaves fights to keep its history alive
rows.standfirst: Despite its status as a historic district, the Tenth Street neighborhood’s history is fading. Residents say a 2010 city ordinance contributed to its decline.

rows.title: State judge temporarily blocks Texas from taking over Houston school district
rows.standfirst: Texas will not be able to seize power of Houston ISD’s school board until the state judge issues a final ruling on the lawsuit challenging the takeover.

rows.title: Add Texas 2020 election dates to your calendar
rows.standfirst: Make it your resolution this year to keep track of voter registration deadlines, early voting and more.

rows.title: Texas revoked a Fort Worth man’s anti-Trump license plate. See what other vanity plates were rejected.
rows.standfirst: The state’s Department of Motor Vehicles revoked the “JAIL 45” plate after someone complained it was offensive.

rows.title: Will Hurd’s legacy casts shadow over Republican primary to replace him in the U.S. House
rows.standfirst: Hurd has endorsed Navy veteran Tony Gonzales in the nine-way GOP primary for the battleground 23rd District.

rows.title: The Texas Tribune: The Next 10 Years
rows.standfirst: In the next 10 years, The Texas Tribune will work to inform and engage even more of our state’s residents. Here’s a look at how we hope to do that.

rows.title: Appeals court rules Trump can use nearly $4 billion in military funds for border wall
rows.standfirst: The White House called the initial decision to block on the use of military funds for the border wall “illegitimate” and hailed the appeals court decision as a victory.

rows.title: Greg Abbott blames another stabbing on Austin’s homeless policies and ramps up DPS patrols
rows.standfirst: The Texas governor said DPS will place additional patrols within two blocks of state buildings downtown and around the University of Texas.

rows.title: UT-Austin acknowledges 17 cases of sexual misconduct by employees
rows.standfirst: Under pressure to more fully account for sexual misconduct cases, the university released a summary of violations over the past two years. The list includes three faculty members.

rows.title: Texas Democrats back resolution to curtail President Trump’s war powers concerning Iran
rows.standfirst: No Texas Republicans in the U.S. House voted for the resolution.

rows.title: Texas leaves the hard work of chasing an accurate census count to communities
rows.standfirst: Local governments, nonprofits and churches are stepping into the organizational void left after Republican Texas lawmakers shot down any significant funding for state efforts to avoid an undercount in the 2020 census.

rows.title: Analysis: Why you should treat elected officials like your dog
rows.standfirst: For four years, local and state governments in Texas were allowed to keep a lot of public business hidden. New laws make more of that information public. But what did they get away with in the meantime?

rows.title: Warren unveils list of new Texas endorsements as presidential race heats up
rows.standfirst: The senator’s backers now include three state representatives, several Texas city council members and local political organizers.

rows.title: Austin to consider stopping arrests, tickets in low-level marijuana cases after hemp law
rows.standfirst: Four progressive members of the City Council are pushing the proposal, which needs two more votes to pass.

rows.title: Under new Texas law, Planned Parenthood likely to be excluded from state employees’ annual charity drive
rows.standfirst: A legal opinion from Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said that facilitating state employees’ donations to Planned Parenthood falls under a 2019 state law prohibiting government entities from entering into “taxpayer resource transactions” with abortion providers or their affiliates.

rows.title: Abbott tells Trump administration Texas won’t participate in refugee resettlement
rows.standfirst: The decision comes after more than 40 other governors said they would opt in to the federal program.

rows.title: With its 228 delegates and Super Tuesday slot, Texas looms in the presidential primary
rows.standfirst: The focus is on the early states, but candidates are also paying attention to Texas. Early voting starts here before the Nevada and South Carolina primaries wrap up.

rows.title: Analysis: A bad day for Planned Parenthood, a good one for Ken Paxton
rows.standfirst: The Texas attorney general got a political gift in the form of a friendly request for his opinion: a chance to take a swipe at a political nemesis.

rows.title: Texas Southern University’s president placed on administrative leave without explanation
rows.standfirst: Texas Southern University President Austin Lane told a local news station he did nothing wrong and expects to be fully reinstated or else paid out for the remainder of his contract.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott, a Catholic, draws criticism over new refugee ban from Texas’ Catholic bishops
rows.standfirst: It’s not the first time Abbott has disagreed with the religious groups over state policy. He was also criticized after he made 2017’s Senate Bill 4, an omnibus, state-based immigration enforcement bill, a legislative priority.

rows.title: As drought persists, Texas ranchers take stock
rows.standfirst: In parts of Texas experiencing severe droughts, some ranchers are finding there is practically no grass left for cattle to graze on.

rows.title: Trump administration sets into motion return of online 3D gun blueprints
rows.standfirst: An Austin man posted blueprints for the world’s first fully 3D-printed gun online in 2013. They’ve been blocked from the internet twice.

rows.title: Texas education officials weigh new rules to fast-track charter school expansion
rows.standfirst: Teachers groups and some education advocates are criticizing the proposed changes, saying more charter schools will siphon money and students away from traditional public schools.

rows.title: Texas oil and gas industry could see a major slowdown in 2020
rows.standfirst: The Texas Oil and Gas Association reported that companies paid a record level of taxes and state royalties last year amid a historic oil boom. But association President Todd Staples said that continued growth is not guaranteed.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg announces plans to hire more than 100 Texas organizers by end of the month
rows.standfirst: The numbers give Bloomberg, the billionaire former mayor of New York City, by far the biggest formal operation in Texas ahead of the state’s March 3 primary.

rows.title: Round two of fight over online voter registration for Texas drivers reaches federal court
rows.standfirst: The state won the first round on a technicality. Now disenfranchised voters are again asking that they be allowed to complete their voter registrations through the online driver’s license portal.

rows.title: Texas carries out nation’s first execution of 2020 for domestic violence slaying in Collin County
rows.standfirst: John Gardner, 64, was put to death for the 2005 murder of his estranged wife. His lawyers had argued the crime wasn’t eligible for the death penalty.

rows.title: Program offering legal help to asylum seekers stuck in Mexico launches in El Paso and Ciudad Juárez
rows.standfirst: Only about 2% of people seeking asylum have access to attorneys, but those with legal representation are much more likely to obtain protections.

rows.title: Analysis: Conservatism, without George W. Bush’s modifier
rows.standfirst: The governor’s decision to opt out of the federal refugee resettlement program marks a shift in the state’s Republican establishment over the last two decades.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas Catholic bishops are critical, but in the pews, immigration views are split
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott’s decision to opt out of the federal refugee program is unpopular with Catholic bishops, but might find more favor among Republicans in Catholic congregations.

rows.title: Three Texas towns vote in favor of “sanctuary cities for the unborn,” hoping to ban abortion
rows.standfirst: Big Spring, Colorado City and Rusk are the three latest towns to vote in favor of such ordinances, which are of contested legality and enforceability.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Sylvia Garcia of Houston one of seven named to prosecution team in Senate impeachment trial
rows.standfirst: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi indicated that she leaned on Garcia for her judicial background.

rows.title: Federal judge blocks policy that allowed Gov. Greg Abbott to ban refugees in Texas
rows.standfirst: The decision comes just days after the Texas governor became the first state leader to opt out of the program. The move drew a harsh rebuke from Texas’ Catholic bishops.

rows.title: Advocates have long tried to change judicial selection in Texas. Is Dan Patrick their newest obstacle?
rows.standfirst: A new commission had barely begun to study Texas’ partisan judicial election system when the leader of the Texas Senate signaled skepticism of reform.

rows.title: TribCast: Refugee ban, hemp fiasco and another Planned Parenthood fight
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Jolie and Emma about the governor’s decision to opt out of the federal refugee resettlement program, the state’s hemp legalization fiasco and the latest in the Texas vs. Planned Parenthood fight.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Dell Medical School’s vice dean talks about fixing health care
rows.standfirst: Watch Mini Kahlon, the vice dean of the University of Texas at Austin’s Dell Medical School, talk about an opportunity for radical change when it comes to health care. Kahlon’s speech is part of a Tribune series on the next 10 years of Texas.

rows.title: In San Antonio, rent is rising but wages aren’t
rows.standfirst: The city already has some of the worst poverty and segregation rates in the country. Now increasing rents are leaving low-income households struggling to keep up with the cost of living.

rows.title: T-Squared: Meet the Pulitzer Prize winner who’ll lead our new investigative team
rows.standfirst: Manny García, a veteran reporter and editor, is the first of 11 hires for our ambitious joint project with ProPublica.

rows.title: Texas Sens. Ted Cruz and John Cornyn back new North American trade deal to replace NAFTA
rows.standfirst: While passage was uncertain at times, the Texas delegation ended up unanimously supporting the international agreement that will replace the North American Free Trade Agreement.

rows.title: New campaign finance reports help crystallize fight for state House majority
rows.standfirst: The reports, which were due Wednesday, provide the first fundraising checkpoint since the candidate fields were finalized last month.

rows.title: Analysis: A seasonal change in Texas politics, as November trumps March
rows.standfirst: For a long time, the party primary elections in Texas have been more competitive than the general elections in November. Not anymore.

rows.title: Texan Ken Starr joins Donald Trump’s impeachment defense team
rows.standfirst: Starr was president of Baylor University during a time when the school was rocked by sexual assault scandals.

rows.title: Texas Southern University regents link president’s ouster to alleged admissions improprieties
rows.standfirst: The board’s statement does not directly tie President Austin Lane to the alleged problems but says he was interviewed before he was placed on leave.

rows.title: A ballot box found weeks after Election Day has flipped a $569 million school bond vote in Midland
rows.standfirst: County officials announced the results for the fourth time Friday.

rows.title: “The farmers are sticking with Trump”: President touts new trade deal during Austin speech
rows.standfirst: The president also exuded confidence that Texas will remain in Republican hands in 2020, despite some political watchers suggesting it’s more purple than it has been in years.

rows.title: In Houston congressional district, Republicans see a chance to boost party diversity and reflip a seat
rows.standfirst: U.S. Rep. Lizzie Pannill Fletcher won Texas’ 7th Congressional District for the Democrats in 2018. Republicans are vying for a chance to win it back.

rows.title: Analysis: Voters elect Texas’ judges. The state might take that power — but it’s risky.
rows.standfirst: Even the Texas lawmakers who want to change the way the state selects judges are wary of taking that power away from voters. The politics are more difficult, in some ways, than the proposed policy changes.

rows.title: Trump names U.S. Rep. John Ratcliffe to advisory and advocacy role during impeachment trial
rows.standfirst: The Heath Republican was an outspoken defender of President Donald Trump during impeachment hearings in the U.S. House last year.

rows.title: Meet the Texas-based church security business training worshippers to fight back in mass shootings
rows.standfirst: Texas has seen two mass shootings in churches in three years, which has some churchgoers exploring training programs to take down an attacker.

rows.title: Big bucks — and a big donor — fuel Allen West’s bid for Texas GOP chair
rows.standfirst: West has raised more than 25 times what incumbent James Dickey has — and more than half of West’s haul came from conservative megadonor Richard Uihlein.

rows.title: Warren reveals more endorsements from former Castro, O’Rourke supporters
rows.standfirst: The Massachusetts U.S. senator’s latest endorsements come from four state lawmakers who represent O’Rourke’s native El Paso and previously supported him or Castro.

rows.title: In 2020 and Beyond, Here’s How to Protect More Injured Texas Workers
rows.standfirst: If you are a Texas employer that does not have workers’ compensation insurance, you should become a QCARE program sponsor.

rows.title: Elizabeth Warren backs Eliz Markowitz in battleground Texas House race
rows.standfirst: The U.S. senator from Massachusetts is the latest Democratic presidential candidate to get involved in the Jan. 28 special election runoff for House District 28.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg’s Texas strategy is expensive and unprecedented. Can it work?
rows.standfirst: Bloomberg is skipping the early states and hoping his big staff and big spending in states like Texas can launch him to victory.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says Texas nonprofits helping refugees should focus on homelessness. Refugee groups say it doesn’t work that way.
rows.standfirst: “Resettlement funding cannot simply be reallocated to other problem areas such as homelessness,” said the CEO of the Lutheran Immigration and Refugee Service.

rows.title: Analysis: Cheating spoils the results — in baseball, and in Texas politics
rows.standfirst: Cheating ruins victory, creating questions about what might have happened. It’s true in sports, and it’s true in politics, too.

rows.title: Obama cut women’s health money in Texas for the state’s targeting of Planned Parenthood. Trump just restored it.
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration announcement reverses an Obama-era decision in 2012 to cut federal women’s health funding to Texas. That came as punishment after the Texas Legislature excluded Planned Parenthood from the Healthy Texas Women program in 2011.

rows.title: TribCast: The money fight for the Texas House and a very special election
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Cassi and Patrick about what we learned from recent campaign finance reports, a nationally targeted special election runoff for a Texas House seat, and presidential endorsements.

rows.title: Texas A&M chancellor fires back at Harvard over criticism of controversial beef study
rows.standfirst: John Sharp sent Harvard’s president an open letter calling for an investigation into Harvard scientists whose actions he said “are false and harmful to Texas A&M University and its faculty.”

rows.title: CBD products are everywhere in Texas since the state legalized hemp. Experts warn: buyer beware.
rows.standfirst: Much of the sudden spike in popularity is thanks to a Texas law last year that legalized hemp, the plant from which CBD is derived.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Texas’ health commissioner talks about preparing for the next decade
rows.standfirst: Watch Dr. Courtney N. Phillips, the state’s health commissioner, talk about some of the challenges for the Texas Health and Human Services Commission. Phillips’ speech is part of a Tribune series on the next 10 years of Texas.

rows.title: With GOP supermajority at risk in 2020, Dan Patrick says Texas Senate may lower threshold to bring bills to the floor
rows.standfirst: The lieutenant governor said Thursday he may decrease the threshold to a simple majority if Republicans lose one or two seats in November.

rows.title: Texas A&M student suspected of contracting deadly coronavirus has been quarantined in Brazos County
rows.standfirst: The virus has killed 25 people outside of the United States so far, according to multiple news organizations.

rows.title: Sen. Ted Cruz launches daily podcast about Trump impeachment trial
rows.standfirst: In the podcast, Cruz reacts to what he’s seen in the trial and makes the case for defending the president.

rows.title: Tom Steyer hires a Texas state director
rows.standfirst: He’s the fourth Democratic presidential candidate who’s still in the race to announce such a hire.

rows.title: Austin police will stop arrests, tickets in most low-level marijuana cases after unanimous City Council vote
rows.standfirst: The decision to back away from pursuing criminal charges against people with small amounts of pot comes after state lawmakers legalized hemp last year in a way that threw marijuana prosecution into chaos.

rows.title: Despite Trump endorsement, Kay Granger’s primary shows no signs of cooling
rows.standfirst: The anti-tax Club for Growth on Thursday backed the Fort Worth congresswoman’s primary challenger, Chris Putnam, ensuring that the race will remain action-packed even after she secured the president’s backing last month.

rows.title: Voting in Texas on Super Tuesday: Everything you need to know
rows.standfirst: Primary election day is March 3. Here’s an overview of everything you need to know about casting a ballot in Texas.

rows.title: Watch interviews with five Democratic candidates running for the U.S. Senate in 2020
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune interviewed MJ Hegar, Chris Bell, Royce West, Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez and Amanda Edwards about the race to challenge U.S. Sen. John Cornyn.

rows.title: Analysis: A special election to test the red-blue shift in Texas politics
rows.standfirst: The winner of the special election underway in Fort Bend County might never take a legislative vote. But House District 28 is an important battleground for Democrats and Republicans fighting over suburban Texas.

rows.title: Attorney general tells Galveston City Council it can’t stop gun shops from locating near schools and churches
rows.standfirst: A letter from the attorney general’s office threatened to sue the city of Galveston if the regulations on gun stores weren’t repealed.

rows.title: Austin police chief: We will still ticket, arrest for marijuana
rows.standfirst: The day after the Austin City Council unanimously approved stopping arrests and tickets for low-level marijuana cases, police Chief Brian Manley said he will continue to enforce such laws.

rows.title: Muddy shoes and difficult questions: How volunteers are counting the number of homeless Texans
rows.standfirst: Hundreds of people walked the streets of Dallas on Thursday to count how many homeless residents live in the area. Similar counts are planned in other cities this month. The results will be key to finding solutions for vulnerable Texans.

rows.title: Baylor student becomes second person in Texas suspected of contracting coronavirus
rows.standfirst: According to an Austin media report, state officials are investigating a potential third case. This week, a student at Texas A&M became the first person in Texas suspected of contracting coronavirus.

rows.title: Texas A&M student does not have coronavirus, health officials say
rows.standfirst: The student recently traveled to Wuhan, China, where the deadly virus originated.

rows.title: Democrats confront bellwether expectations as Texas House special election reaches end
rows.standfirst: Texas House District 28 is getting wide attention from Democrats, but it is far from the most competitive legislative district on their radar this year, and Republicans are confident ahead of a special election runoff Tuesday.

rows.title: Analysis: The Texas Senate could become more democratic — for partisan reasons
rows.standfirst: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says he might adjust Senate rules if the GOP majority shrinks — the better to bring Republican legislation up for debate when Democrats object. What’s so surprising about that?

rows.title: Texas officials say all four suspected coronavirus cases tested negative
rows.standfirst: Health officials said Monday that there were no confirmed cases in the state.

rows.title: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to proceed with immigration rules
rows.standfirst: The rules establish new criteria for who can be considered to be dependent on the U.S. government for benefits and thus ineligible for green cards and a path to U.S. citizenship.

rows.title: Texas State Technical College bought furniture from store owned by CFO and his wife
rows.standfirst: College officials say there was no impropriety because their chief financial officer disclosed the conflict and had no say in the furniture purchased from the family store. An internal audit cleared the school and CFO of wrongdoing.

rows.title: CBD, hemp, medical marijuana? Here’s what you need to know about Texas’ changing pot laws.
rows.standfirst: Marijuana and hemp are often indistinguishable by look or smell because they both come from the cannabis plant. But hemp is legal, and marijuana is not.

rows.title: UT-Austin students condemn school’s handling of sexual misconduct cases
rows.standfirst: “You’re not trying to help us,” university President Greg Fenves and other administrators were told at an emotional public meeting called after months of campus protests.

rows.title: Bernie Sanders campaign homes in on Texas as primary nears
rows.standfirst: The Democratic presidential candidate is expanding its efforts in the state a little over a month before Texas’ delegate-rich primary.

rows.title: Republican Gary Gates handily beats Democrat Eliz Markowitz in Texas House District 28 runoff
rows.standfirst: Democrats had hoped the race would build momentum for their push to take control of the Texas House in November. The Houston-area contest garnered national attention and overshadowed two other special election runoffs for House districts Tuesday.

rows.title: How U.S. Rep. Sylvia Garcia of Houston landed in the middle of Donald Trump’s impeachment
rows.standfirst: Decades of nuts-and-bolts political work and a friendship with House Speaker Nancy Pelosi landed the first-term congresswoman a starring role in the Senate trial of President Trump.

rows.title: Conservative activists helped elect Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick. Now some say there’s a disconnect.
rows.standfirst: A group of hardline grassroots activists has called on Patrick to be more outspoken on party priorities and worries that lines of communication appear to no longer be there.

rows.title: Analysis: Testing the Texas political waters by breaking the rules
rows.standfirst: Break the political rules and lose, you’re a footnote. But break them and win, and the whole game changes. Michael Bloomberg is the latest candidate to try on the presidential stage.

rows.title: Bernie Sanders endorses Jessica Cisneros, primary challenger to Henry Cuellar
rows.standfirst: Cisneros was one of nine candidates Sanders endorsed early Wednesday, in addition to incumbent Democratic Reps. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota and Peter Welch of Vermont.

rows.title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton won’t defend state agency in gay marriage case
rows.standfirst: The attorney general’s office is charged with defending state agencies when they are challenged in court. But Paxton will not defend a commission sued after it issued a public warning for a Waco judge who refuses to perform same-sex marriages.

rows.title: Analysis: In special Texas House election, Democrats bit off more than they could chew
rows.standfirst: Texas Democrats raised the stakes in their effort to flip a Republican House seat to their side in Fort Bend County. It was a long-shot, promoted as a promising opportunity. And they lost, big.

rows.title: Cornyn has $12 million for reelection bid after raising $2.8 million in fourth quarter
rows.standfirst: Cornyn will face the winner of a crowded Democratic primary. That group of hopefuls includes MJ Hegar, who announced Tuesday that she raised $1.1 million over the past three months.

rows.title: TribCast: A special election blowout and checking in on the presidential primary
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Matthew talks to Alex, Cassi and Patrick about the big Republican win in House District 28, growing unrest among grassroots conservatives and the state of the presidential primary in Texas.

rows.title: Ahead of explosion, Port Neches plant reported an increase of rogue emissions of explosive gas
rows.standfirst: After the federal government required TPC Group to install air monitors at its Port Neches plant, the company detected a significant increase in the number and size of butadiene emissions in the months leading up to multiple blasts at the plant on Nov. 27.

rows.title: Democrats regroup after Republicans score easy win in Texas House special election
rows.standfirst: Campaign strategies — and the extent of Beto O’Rourke’s involvement — were being contemplated after a big loss in a race that gained statewide attention.

rows.title: Migrants, advocates mark the anniversary of “remain in Mexico” with fear, anger and trepidation
rows.standfirst: As lawmakers, immigration attorneys and advocates call for the end of the Migrant Protection Protocols, the Department of Homeland Security announced it would expand to include Brazilians.

rows.title: Texas officials on the coronavirus: Keep calm and wash your hands
rows.standfirst: On Thursday, the World Health Organization declared the coronavirus a public health emergency. But officials say the flu is still a bigger threat in Texas.

rows.title: Trump plans to collect DNA from nearly a million immigrants despite charges it violates privacy
rows.standfirst: Pilot projects could lead to the Trump administration storing genetic material from children as young as 14 years old in the name of fighting crime.

rows.title: More Texas renters are struggling to find affordable housing, new report finds
rows.standfirst: Experts say that as more high-income Texans rent, prices on existing homes are driven up. Meanwhile, the number of expensive units in the state is increasing as more affordable homes disappear.

rows.title: Analysis: Fort Bend’s special election was just the first battle of the 2020 war between Texas Democrats and Republicans
rows.standfirst: The Republican elation and Democratic misery over this week’s special election in Fort Bend County is just the first wave of the 2020 election year. The parties have dozens of challenges ahead of them.

rows.title: University of Texas’ poorest incoming freshmen to receive $20,000, laptops and more starting this fall
rows.standfirst: The Dell Foundation’s $100 million gift to the University of Texas is a 10-year commitment to provide funds and services to Pell Grant recipients.

rows.title: Stepping into GOP primaries, Dennis Bonnen donates to seven Texas House incumbents
rows.standfirst: The contributions mark the first notable movement from Bonnen’s PAC since he announced in October he wasn’t seeking reelection.

rows.title: Ted Cruz, John Cornyn join most GOP senators in voting against new witnesses in impeachment trial
rows.standfirst: The decision on witnesses comes after two weeks of arguments inside the Senate chamber from Democratic impeachment managers and the president’s defense team.
